sealed.statement: The shipped lagrange service init <directory> command atomically creates a deterministic non-overwriting OCI-container Node service source project and a version-1 external-manifest template that intentionally omits artifact.digest until S5b builds the OCI layout, while initialization performs no cluster, SQL, WebSocket, catalog, or runtime work.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

package.json exposes lagrange through src/sea-entry.js, which routes the top-level service command before loading the server and preserves existing global help, version, and lagrange-admin behavior. The service router is the sole extension point for later S5b and S5c commands; no AdminCLI or WebSocket control path is added.

Initialization emits lagrange-service.template.json as valid JSON with schema_version 1, OCI artifact metadata, and oci_container runtime metadata, but artifact.digest is absent. The existing external-manifest owner must reject the template only for the required digest and accept the same document after a valid digest is supplied; no fake or placeholder digest may be emitted.

The command writes a fixed path set with byte-identical content for the same project name, uses no timestamps, randomness, or environment-derived content, creates the target directory exclusively, cleans up only a target it created after a write failure, and never modifies an existing file, directory, or symlink.

The scaffold contains an executable and tested Node service, a Dockerfile pinned to the repository's approved Node OCI image digest, and OCI image-manifest media metadata. It exposes no wasm_component or native_js template option.

Initialization is local filesystem work only: production code must not import or invoke cluster, SQL, PG-wire, WebSocket, admin, catalog, reconciler, runtime, network, subprocess, dependency-install, or artifact-resolution owners.

S5a hands S5b only generated source files and lagrange-service.template.json. It must not create oci-layout, index.json, blobs, a final lagrange-service.json, an artifact digest, a build command, a dev-install command, or any resolver-specific intermediate interface.

The scenario must exercise the package-declared shipped entrypoint and bundled SEA entry, generated service tests and health response, deterministic bytes, template rejection and post-digest acceptance, missing and extra arguments, unknown commands/options, invalid project names, existing targets, and symlink targets. It must also prove service help exits without loading the server.

Production scope is package.json, package-lock.json, src/sea-entry.js, and dedicated src/cli service-command and service-project-scaffold modules. Proof scope is test/cli/service-init-scaffold.test.js, test/packaging/sea-bundle-smoke.test.js, and scripts/checks/run-service-init-scaffold-scenarios.js. No other production owner is in scope.

Independent verification must show the declared scenario fails when shipped entrypoint routing or atomic no-clobber behavior is reverted, and must verify the exact source patch plus aggregate content before checkpoint and handoff.

hypothesis: Add the shipped local service command router and an atomic deterministic OCI Node scaffold with a truthful digest-less template and bundled-entrypoint adversarial proof.

claim: Independent exact verification passed for the canonical six-path product patch: three scenario samples and static gates were green, while routing and no-clobber regression controls were red.
Independent post-checkpoint aggregate verification passed for the unchanged canonical six-path product scope and reused complete exact evidence.
